newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids firm on higher crude, HSFO interest.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids firm on higher crude, HSFO interest.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices firmed Thursday on higher crude futures and continued strong interest in the high-sulphur materials, especially in the Gulf Coast.
There were talks that a few East Coast utilities showed interests to purchase spot fuel oil supplies for April delivery, according to market sources.
"At last we're starting to see incremental barrel demand," said a Northeast-based physical trader, but cautioned there is supply in inventory to meet a rise in spot demand.
"Oil is there. People are just sitting on it," he added.
NYH one percent physical rose to $16.00-25 a barrel from yesterday's $15.85-16.15. One percent NYH paper firmed to $15.90-16.10 from $15.75-16.00 Wednesday with a late rise in NYMEX crude futures.
The NYMEX April crude contract settled up 28 cents at $22.32 a bbl, trimming a 46 cent gain.
NYH HSFO prices were steady with three percent gaining 25 cents to $13.25-75. The 0.3 percent high pour held at $17.00.
In the U.S. Gulf, three percent sulphur grade jumped 25-75 cents to $14.25-75 on reported sales at $14.70 and 14.80. Three percent paper widened to $13.90-14.25 from $14.00-20 Wednesday.
USG one percent physical rose about 25 cent to $14.75/bbl.
At the New York City gate, day-ahead natural gas slipped again, down to $2.21-2.28 per million British thermal units or $14.18 a barrel equivalent from Wednesday's $2.30-2.32/mmBtu or $14.55/bbl.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, held steady at $1.87/mmBtu or 11.78/bbl equivalent.
